citations.narrative:
On August 19, 2026, a search was conducted at the facility because there is evidence that the owner is conducting
regulated activity without a license. On June 12, 2026, the facility owner sold 2 badgers for use as pets to a USDA
licensed broker who then sold the badgers to a USDA licensee who sells exotic pets. On July 9, 2026, the facility owner
posted 6 skunks for sale on an online swap site. During today’s inspection, there were breeding pairs of skunks, ground
hogs, badgers, and opossums. The owner is renovating enclosures and has built a perimeter fence in preparation for
licensing but admitted he had sold the badgers and skunks as pets this year before he could complete those preparations.
Badgers, skunks, ground hogs and opossums are defined as “wild animals’ under the Animal Welfare Act. Selling wild
animals as pets is an activity that requires a valid license under the Animal Welfare Act. A license must be obtained prior
to conducting further regulated activity.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
